arcs.motif: one global coherence compatible with real local difference
formalTargets: natural transformation across the Jordan-to-device chain
arcs.minimalAnsatz: A sheaf of local action, module and port models with explicit overlap maps and a computed Cech obstruction.
arcs.cheapestKillTest: Test whether the known anomaly, bundle and port obstructions inhabit one common cohomological complex without changing their types.
arcs.negativeControl: Compare against a direct product of three unrelated obstruction complexes with the same parameter count.
arcs.beautifulResult: Anomaly cancellation, family-bundle gluing and calibrated response become boundary maps of one descent problem.
arcs.failureValue: Proves the obstructions are genuinely heterogeneous and prevents a false unification.

arcs.motif: three irreducible roles related without becoming three copies
formalTargets: cyclic operad with a nontrivial coherence cell
arcs.minimalAnsatz: Define a typed ternary operation whose outer slots are wall endpoints and whose middle slot is the charged mediator; calculate its stabilizer and rephasing weight.
arcs.cheapestKillTest: Check whether the operation factors through a binary associative envelope or retains the charge-minus-two Hom obstruction of claim 1463.
arcs.negativeControl: Replace the middle slot by a generic bilinear spurion and compare invariants.
arcs.beautifulResult: Metric, symplectic sewing and phase selection are shadows of one typed ternary relation.
arcs.failureValue: Localizes why poetic threeness does not repair the physical charge grading.

arcs.motif: a universal structure realized locally without losing its global identity
arcs.minimalAnsatz: Construct one functor taking the Spin(2,3) projector orbit and parent representation to O(3) selected modes plus O(0) heavy spectators.
arcs.cheapestKillTest: Determine whether functoriality alone distinguishes O(3) from O(0), or whether the split must be inserted as independent matter data.
arcs.negativeControl: Apply the same construction to O(k) plus O(0) for k not equal to three.
arcs.beautifulResult: The family index and anomaly-free spectator sector arise from one canonical defect map.
arcs.failureValue: Turns the missing asymmetric bundle assignment into a precise no-natural-transformation theorem.

arcs.motif: a symmetric law permits an orbit while history selects and remembers one member
formalTargets: hysteretic stochastic preparation on a vacuum orbit
determinant-line orientation fixed by a boundary history
arcs.minimalAnsatz: Introduce one operational history variable and test whether it jointly selects wall orientation, sterile phase and charged TRO without a free complex coefficient.
arcs.cheapestKillTest: Perform the full rephasing quotient; kill the arc if the shared history correlation is gauge removable or not reversibly preparable.
arcs.negativeControl: Independent random preparation of the three orientations with identical marginals.
arcs.beautifulResult: One measurable preparation history supplies the transforming datum demanded by the equivariant-selection theorem.
arcs.failureValue: Separates physical memory from relabeling and closes a large class of narrative selectors.

arcs.motif: disappearance and return with conserved identity carried through a crossing
formalTargets: domain-wall kernel transport through a phase transition
arcs.minimalAnsatz: Choose a one-parameter family of parent Dirac operators; calculate spectral flow, endpoint representations and Pfaffian orientation.
arcs.cheapestKillTest: Check whether the index fixes anything beyond net mode number, especially Standard Model representation, mass or phase.
arcs.negativeControl: A homotopic operator loop with the same net index but scrambled endpoint representation data.
arcs.beautifulResult: Three families are protected memory of a passage rather than three static copies.
arcs.failureValue: Shows exactly which phenomenological data index theory cannot carry.

arcs.sourceClass: Ophanim, visionary recursion and altered-state geometry
arcs.motif: nested rotations, self-similar tilings and observer-relative rendering
formalTargets: renormalization or substitution system on positive response cones
nested commutant tower with scale-dependent dilations
arcs.minimalAnsatz: Define a coarse-graining map on two-port positive matrices and ask whether its noncompact symmetry closure converges uniquely to Sp(4,R).
arcs.cheapestKillTest: Run random substitution and random-network baselines; kill the arc if Sp(4) closure is generic, basis-induced or lacks a held-out scale invariant.
arcs.negativeControl: Degree-preserving random graphs and shuffled substitution rules.
arcs.beautifulResult: The same Spin(2,3) response geometry is a unique attractive fixed point across microscopic and macroscopic scales.
arcs.failureValue: Quantifies apophenia risk and distinguishes self-similar pictures from invariant dynamics.

arcs.motif: one invariant becomes expressible in several languages while their distinctions remain
formalTargets: Morita or duality equivalence preserving observables
arcs.minimalAnsatz: Specify objects and arrows for Jordan, Furey, defect, effective-action and calibrated-port categories and demand commuting squares for a finite invariant packet.
arcs.cheapestKillTest: Count unconstrained conjugators and free GL maps; kill the bridge if commutativity can always be restored by basis choice.
arcs.negativeControl: A maximally flexible equivalence with one independently fitted map per square.
arcs.beautifulResult: One invariant packet survives the path from Jordan relation to measured device response.
arcs.failureValue: Produces a finite list of the exact squares that do not commute.

arcs.motif: compression and naturality can guide attention without guaranteeing truth
formalTargets: Pareto ranking of compression, naturality and falsifiability
arcs.minimalAnsatz: Score competing typed ansatze before examining a held-out consequence, with penalties for parameters, type debt and post-hoc repair.
arcs.cheapestKillTest: Blind the source story and test whether the ranking predicts held-out constraints better than complexity-matched random rankings.
arcs.negativeControl: Numerology and relabeling families tuned to equal in-sample beauty scores.
arcs.beautifulResult: The shortest natural construction compresses several independently derived facts and predicts one new invariant.
arcs.failureValue: Calibrates beauty as a cognitive prior and exposes when it rewards only redescription.
